title: Protocol for high-throughput compound screening using flow cytometry in THP-1 cells
protocol: Culture THP-1 cells in suspension in T75 or T150 flasks.
Move cells to T225 flasks when 50 mL or greater of cell culture is achieved.
Maintain cells between 300,000 and 800,000 cells per mL in THP-1 culture media.
Dilute cells with media when they approach 800,000 cells per mL.
Mix cells well before taking a sample to determine cell density.
Dilute a sample of cell suspension in a 1:1 ratio with 0.4% Trypan Blue solution.
Load 10 μl of cell suspension with Trypan Blue onto a hemocytometer or automated cell counter slide.
Count cells using the hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Dilute cells with fresh media to 300,000 cells per mL.
Passage cells with a complete media exchange approximately 3–4 days later.
Mix cells well and take a sample to count cells using 0.4% Trypan Blue and a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend in fresh media at 300,000 cells per mL.
Titrate IFN-γ activity by performing a dose response curve with at least 12 concentrations of IFN-γ and at least 10 replicate wells for each concentration.
Centrifuge THP-1 cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in fresh media at 1.25 million viable cells per mL.
Distribute 40 μl of cell suspension per well to a 384 well plate using a reagent dispenser or multichannel pipette.
Prepare dilution of IFN-γ at 5X of its desired final concentration.
Dilute IFN-γ in THP-1 media starting at 10 μg/mL.
Perform serial dilutions by a factor of 2 to generate at least 12 concentrations, with the final concentration being approximately 4.9 ng/mL IFN-γ.
Transfer diluted IFN-γ to cell wells using a multichannel pipette.
Add 10 μl per well for a final well volume of 50 μl and include 50,000 cells per well.
Ensure each dilution has at least 10 replicate wells.
Add 10 μl of media without IFN-γ to a set of 10 replicate wells as an unstimulated control.
Incubate cells in a standard humidified 37°C 5% CO2 incubator for three days.
Proceed with staining and flow cytometry analysis starting from step 21.
Graph the median fluorescence intensity of PD-L1 vs IFN-γ concentration on a log scale.
Generate a dose response curve using GraphPad Prism or similar program.
Calculate EC20 and EC50 for IFN-γ using "[Agonist] vs. Response - Find ECanything" method in GraphPad Prism.
Remove compound source plates from the freezer at least 2 hours before planned use to allow equilibration to approximately 20°C.
Ensure plates are well sealed with an aluminum seal when removed from and returned to cold storage.
Mix compound source plates well by vortexing at high speed with the HT-91002 microplate orbital shaker for at least 1 minute.
Centrifuge mixed compound plates at approximately 20–25°C for 10 minutes at 1000 × g to ensure no compound remains on aluminum foil seals.
Mix THP-1 cells well with a hemocytometer and 0.4% Trypan Blue.
Count viable THP-1 cells using the hemocytometer and Trypan Blue.
Calculate the number of cells needed for the screen, requiring 21 million viable cells per full 384 well plate.
Measure out sufficient THP-1 cells for the screen based on the calculated amount.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in fresh culture media to achieve a concentration of 1 million cells per mL (21 mL per screening plate).
Pipette 1 mL of resuspended THP-1 cells into each separate centrifuge tube for unstimulated controls.
Add IFN-γ to the main tube of cells to a concentration equivalent to the EC20 of activation as determined in the previous IFN-γ titration section.
Mix well by inverting the tube or pipetting up and down 5 to 10 times.
Distribute IFN-γ stimulated cells to the first 23 columns of the black 384 well assay plates, 50 μl per well (50,000 cells per well).
Distribute unstimulated cells to column 24 at 50 μl per well.
Label or barcode cell plates clearly matched to compound source plates.
Transfer 100 nl of compound from the compound source plate to the cell plate using BioMek FX.
Seal compound plate with a new aluminum foil seal.
Incubate cells at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Incubate cells for 3 days with IFN-γ and compounds.
Centrifuge cell plates for 5 minutes at 300 × g at 4°C.
Remove vials of Fixable Viability Dye (Thermo Fisher Scientific) 660 from the freezer to allow them to thaw to approximately 20°C.
Aspirate supernatant with a plate washer, leaving a thin layer of supernatant covering the pelleted cells.
Wash cells by dispensing 80 μl cold DPBS without calcium or magnesium per well.
Centrifuge and aspirate supernatant.
Keep plates on ice or refrigerated from this point onwards.
Cells are initially washed with DPBS, not FACS buffer, to reduce background staining of the viability dye.
While the cells are centrifuging, mix viability dye concentrate by vortexing.
Briefly spin down the tube with a benchtop microcentrifuge.
Ensure the viability dye has completely thawed.
Dilute the viability dye 1:1000 in cold PBS.
Prepare 16 mL per plate plus an extra 5 mL to account for the dead volume of the reagent dispenser tubing.
Dispense 40 μl diluted viability dye per well after the second wash cycle with DPBS, cells have been centrifuged and supernatant aspirated.
Vortex each plate without a lid using HT-91002 microplate orbital shaker at speed setting 700 for about 5 seconds to resuspend the cells.
Incubate plates at 4°C in the dark with gentle rocking or orbital shaking for 30 minutes.

Gradually increase the speed on an HT-91002 microplate orbital shaker or equivalent until the plate can be shaken vigorously enough to resuspend cells without spilling contents, ensuring thorough mixing by observation with a standard light microscope.
Dilute Human FcR Blocking Reagent 1:20 in FACS buffer, preparing approximately 6 mL per plate for use at 15 μl per well.
Aspirate supernatant from plates after centrifugation and dispense 15 μl diluted Human FcR Blocking Reagent per well.
Vortex plates without lids using the shaker set to speed setting 700 for 5 to 10 seconds each.
Incubate plates at 4°C with gentle rocking or orbital shaking in the dark for 10 minutes.
Prepare antibody dilutions during the incubation period.
Dilute PE conjugated anti-human PD-L1 antibody 1:60 in FACS buffer for an ultimate dilution of approximately 1:150.
Ensure enough volume is prepared for 15 μl per well (approximately 6 ml per plate with dead volume).
Dispense 15 μl per well of diluted antibody without centrifuging the plates.
Vortex plates without lids using the plate shaker at speed setting 700 for 5 to 10 seconds each.
Incubate plates at 4°C with gentle rocking or orbital shaking in the dark for 45 minutes.
Dispense 40 μl per well of FACS buffer following the 45-minute incubation.
Centrifuge plates.
Aspirate supernatant, dispense 80 μl per well FACS buffer.
Centrifuge plates.
Aspirate supernatant, vortex plates without lids using the plate shaker at speed setting 700 for 5 to 10 seconds each.
Dispense 40 μl per well 4% paraformaldehyde diluted from a 32% stock in DPBS.
Incubate for 15 minutes at approximately 20°C, with gentle rocking or orbital shaking, protecting plates from light.
Dispense 40 μl per well FACS buffer.
Centrifuge plates, aspirate supernatant, and vortex plates to resuspend cells.
Dispense 50 μl per well FACS buffer.
Vortex plates again to ensure cells are resuspended and well mixed.
Analyze a few control wells before mass analysis to ensure the flow cytometer is working properly.
Set gates on FSC-A vs. SSC-A to identify cells and eliminate debris.
Set gates on FSC-H vs. FSC-A or FSC-H vs. Pulse Width to eliminate doublets.
Set gates on APC-A vs. FSC-A to gate on viable cells, with Fixable viability dye 660 detected in the APC channel.
Determine PD-L1+ cells using PE-A vs. FSC-A or PE-A histogram.
Use no IFN-γ and/or IFN-γ + vehicle control wells to determine gates for PD-L1 high or low expression.
Acquire all wells in one plate continuously, storing data as a single FCS file.
Pump speed: 15 rpm.
Prime with sheath fluid for 60 seconds.
Pre-shake for 15 seconds at 3500 rpm.
Sample acquisition time: 7 seconds.
Up time: 3 seconds.
Rinse probe after every 12 wells with FACS clean solution and water for 1 second each.
Shake sample well after every 12 wells for 4 seconds at 3500 rpm.
Perform post run flush with sheath fluid for 60 seconds.
